sanskrit: ye bhakṣayanti māṃsāni bhūtānāṃ jīvitaiṣiṇām bhakṣyante te 'pi tair bhūtair iti me nāsti saṃśayaḥ
english: Those who eat the flesh of creatures that long to live shall themselves be eaten by those very creatures—of this I have no doubt.

sanskrit: māṃ sa bhakṣayate yasmād bhakṣayiṣye tam apy aham etan māṃsasya māṃsatvam ato budhyasva bhārata
english: "Since he devours me, I too shall devour him"—this is the very flesh-nature of flesh; understand it thus, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ghātako vadhyate nityaṃ tathā vadhyeta bandhakaḥ ākroṣṭākruśyate rājan dveṣṭā dveṣyatvam āpnute
english: The slayer is ever slain in turn, and the binder is bound; the reviler, O king, is reviled, and the hater becomes an object of hatred.

sanskrit: yena yena śarīreṇa yad yat karma karoti yaḥ tena tena śarīreṇa tat tat phalam upāśnute
english: With whatever body a man performs whatever deed, with that very body he reaps its fruit.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā paramo dharmas tathāhiṃsā paro damaḥ ahiṃsā paramaṃ dānam ahiṃsā paramaṃ tapaḥ
english: Non-harming is the highest dharma; non-harming is the highest self-restraint; non-harming is the highest gift; non-harming is the highest austerity.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā paramo yajñas tathāhiṃsā paraṃ balam ahiṃsā paramaṃ mitram ahiṃsā paramaṃ sukham ahiṃsā paramaṃ satyam ahiṃsā paramaṃ śrutam
english: Non-harming is the highest sacrifice; non-harming is the highest strength; non-harming is the highest friend; non-harming is the highest happiness; non-harming is the highest truth; non-harming is the highest sacred lore.

sanskrit: sarvayajñeṣu vā dānaṃ sarvatīrtheṣu cāplutam sarvadānaphalaṃ vāpi naitat tulyam ahiṃsayā
english: Gifts at all sacrifices, bathing at all sacred fords, the fruit of every act of giving—none of these is equal to non-harming.

sanskrit: ahiṃsrasya tapo 'kṣayyam ahiṃsro yajate sadā ahiṃsraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yathā mātā yathā pitā
english: The austerity of the harmless one is imperishable; the harmless one sacrifices unceasingly; the harmless one is to all creatures as a mother, as a father.

sanskrit: etat phalam ahiṃsāyā bhūyaś ca kurupuṃgava na hi śakyā guṇā vaktum iha varṣaśatair api
english: Such is the fruit of non-harming, and more besides, O bull of the Kurus; its virtues could not be told here even in a hundred years.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca akāmāś ca sakāmāś ca hatā ye 'smin mahāhave kāṃ yoniṃ pratipannās te tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Those slain in this great battle, whether unwilling or willing—into what wombs have they passed? Tell me that, grandfather.

sanskrit: duḥkhaṃ prāṇaparityāgaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ mahāmṛdhe jānāmi tattvaṃ dharmajña prāṇatyāgaṃ suduṣkaram
english: The surrender of life by men in great combat is a grievous thing; I know the truth of it, O knower of dharma—giving up one's breath is most hard.

sanskrit: samṛddhe vāsamṛddhe vā śubhe vā yadi vāśubhe kāraṇaṃ tatra me brūhi sarvajño hy asi me mataḥ
english: Whether in prosperity or in ruin, in fortune or in misfortune, tell me the reason for it; for in my judgment you are all-knowing.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca samṛddhe vāsamṛddhe vā śubhe vā yadi vāśubhe saṃsāre 'smin samājātāḥ prāṇinaḥ pṛthivīpate
english: Bhīṣma said: Whether in prosperity or ruin, in fortune or misfortune, living beings are born together into this round of existence, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: niratā yena bhāvena tatra me śṛṇu kāraṇam samyak cāyam anupraśnas tvayoktaś ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: By what disposition they are bound—hear from me the reason for it; and this further question you have asked is well put, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: atra te vartayiṣyāmi purāvṛttam idaṃ nṛpa dvaipāyanasya saṃvādaṃ kīṭasya ca yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this I shall relate to you an ancient happening, O king—the dialogue of Dvaipāyana and a worm, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: brahmabhūtaś caran vipraḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ purā dadarśa kīṭaṃ dhāvantaṃ śīghraṃ śakaṭavartmani
english: Of old, the brāhmaṇa Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, who had become one with Brahman, while wandering, saw a worm running swiftly along a cart-track.

sanskrit: gatijñaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ rutajñaś ca śarīriṇām sarvajñaḥ sarvato dṛṣṭvā kīṭaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: He who knew the ways of all beings and the cries of all embodied creatures, the all-knowing one, seeing the worm before him, spoke these words.

sanskrit: kīṭa saṃtrastarūpo 'si tvaritaś caiva lakṣyase kva dhāvasi tad ācakṣva kutas te bhayam āgatam
english: O worm, you seem terrified and you appear to be in haste; where are you running? Tell me that—whence has fear come upon you?

sanskrit: kīṭa uvāca śakaṭasyāsya mahato ghoṣaṃ śrutvā bhayaṃ mama āgataṃ vai mahābuddhe svana eṣa hi dāruṇaḥ śrūyate na sa māṃ hanyād iti tasmād apākrame
english: The worm said: Hearing the loud rumble of this great cart, fear has come upon me, O greatly wise one; for this din that is heard is terrible. "Let it not crush me"—therefore I flee away.

sanskrit: śvasatāṃ ca śṛṇomy evaṃ goputrāṇāṃ pracodyatām vahatāṃ sumahābhāraṃ saṃnikarṣe svanaṃ prabho nṛṇāṃ ca saṃvāhayatāṃ śrūyate vividhaḥ svanaḥ
english: And thus I hear close by the panting of the goaded oxen as they haul the mighty load, O lord; and the many sounds of the men driving them are heard.

sanskrit: soḍhum asmadvidhenaiṣa na śakyaḥ kīṭayoninā tasmād apakramāmy eṣa bhayād asmāt sudāruṇāt
english: This cannot be endured by one of my kind, born in a worm's womb; therefore I am fleeing away from this most terrible peril.

sanskrit: duḥkhaṃ hi mṛtyur bhūtānāṃ jīvitaṃ ca sudurlabham ato bhītaḥ palāyāmi gaccheyaṃ nāsukhaṃ sukhāt
english: Death is grievous for living beings, and life is very hard to win; therefore, in fear, I flee, that I may not pass from comfort into misery.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tu taṃ prāha kutaḥ kīṭa sukhaṃ tava maraṇaṃ te sukhaṃ manye tiryagyonau hi vartase
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, the sage replied to it: How can there be any comfort for you, O worm? I deem death to be your comfort, for you dwell in the womb of a beast.

sanskrit: śabdaṃ sparśaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ bhogāṃś coccāvacān bahūn nābhijānāsi kīṭa tvaṃ śreyo maraṇam eva te
english: Sound, touch, taste, smell, and the many pleasures high and low—of these, O worm, you have no knowledge; death itself is better for you.

sanskrit: kīṭa uvāca sarvatra nirato jīva itīhāpi sukhaṃ mama cetayāmi mahāprājña tasmād icchāmi jīvitum
english: The worm said: A living creature finds delight in every state, and so even here I have my happiness; I am aware of it, O greatly wise one, and therefore I wish to live.

sanskrit: ihāpi viṣayaḥ sarvo yathādehaṃ pravartitaḥ mānuṣās tiryagāś caiva pṛthagbhogā viśeṣataḥ
english: Even here every realm of sense-objects is set in motion according to the body one has; men and beasts have their separate enjoyments, each in its own kind.

sanskrit: aham āsaṃ manuṣyo vai śūdro bahudhanaḥ purā abrahmaṇyo nṛśaṃsaś ca kadaryo vṛddhijīvanaḥ
english: I was once a man, a śūdra of great wealth, hostile to brāhmaṇas, cruel, miserly, and living by usury.

sanskrit: vāktīkṣṇo nikṛtiprajño moṣṭā viśvasya sarvaśaḥ mithaḥkṛto 'panidhanaḥ parasvaharaṇe rataḥ
english: Sharp of tongue, cunning of mind, a thief of everything from everyone, a breaker of trusts who hid away his deposits, bent on seizing others' goods.

sanskrit: bhṛtyātithijanaś cāpi gṛhe paryuṣito mayā mātsaryāt svādukāmena nṛśaṃsena bubhūṣatā
english: And the servants and guests in my house I let go hungry through the night, out of grudging spite, craving the dainties for myself, cruel and greedy to keep all for my own.

sanskrit: devārthaṃ pitṛyajñārtham annaṃ śraddhākṛtaṃ mayā na dattam arthakāmena deyam annaṃ punāti ha
english: Food prepared with faith for the gods and for the sacrifice to the ancestors I, greedy for gain, did not give away—yet food that ought to be given purifies indeed.

sanskrit: guptaṃ śaraṇam āśritya bhayeṣu śaraṇāgatāḥ akasmān no bhayāt tyaktā na ca trātābhayaiṣiṇaḥ
english: Those who, seeking safety in their fears, took refuge under my protection I abandoned without cause in their terror, nor did I shelter them who sought refuge.

sanskrit: dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ priyān dārān yānaṃ vāsas tathādbhutam śriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā manuṣyāṇām asūyāmi nirarthakam
english: Seeing men's wealth, their grain, their dear wives, their carriages and splendid dwellings and prosperity, I begrudged it all to no purpose.

sanskrit: īrṣyuḥ parasukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā ātatāyy abubhūṣakaḥ trivargahantā cānyeṣām ātmakāmānuvartakaḥ
english: Envious at the sight of others' happiness, an aggressor unwilling to let others thrive, a destroyer of the threefold aim of life in others, following only my own desires.

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsaguṇabhūyiṣṭhaṃ purā karma kṛtaṃ mayā smṛtvā tad anutapye 'haṃ tyaktvā priyam ivātmajam
english: The deeds I did of old were full to overflowing with cruelty; remembering them, I grieve, as one who has lost a beloved son.

sanskrit: śubhānām api jānāmi kṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalam mātā ca pūjitā vṛddhā brāhmaṇaś cārcito mayā
english: Yet I know too the fruit of good deeds I performed: my aged mother I honored, and a brāhmaṇa I revered.

sanskrit: sakṛj jātiguṇopetaḥ saṃgatyā gṛham āgataḥ atithiḥ pūjito brahmaṃs tena māṃ nājahāt smṛtiḥ
english: Once, a guest endowed with high birth and virtue came by chance to my house, and I honored him, O brāhmaṇa; for that reason, memory has not forsaken me.

sanskrit: karmaṇā tena caivāhaṃ sukhāśām iha lakṣaye tac chrotum aham icchāmi tvattaḥ śreyas tapodhana
english: By that deed I look for a hope of happiness even here; I wish to hear from you what is best, O you whose wealth is austerity.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca śubhena karmaṇā yad vai tiryagyonau na muhyase mamaiva kīṭa tat karma yena tvaṃ na pramuhyase
english: Vyāsa said: That through a good deed you are not bewildered even in the womb of a beast—that, O worm, is my own working, by which you are not led astray.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi darśanād eva tārayāmi tapobalāt tapobalād dhi balavad balam anyan na vidyate
english: For by my very sight I deliver you, through the power of austerity; for than the power of austerity there is no other power more mighty.

sanskrit: jānāmi pāpaiḥ svakṛtair gataṃ tvāṃ kīṭa kīṭatām avāpsyasi paraṃ dharmaṃ dharmastho yadi manyase
english: I know that by your own sins you have come, O worm, to the state of a worm; yet you shall attain the highest dharma, if, abiding in dharma, you so resolve.

sanskrit: karma bhūmikṛtaṃ devā bhuñjate tiryagāś ca ye dharmād api manuṣyeṣu kāmo 'rthaś ca yathā guṇaiḥ
english: The deeds wrought upon earth the gods enjoy, and so do the beasts; even more than dharma, among men, do pleasure and gain accrue according to one's qualities.

sanskrit: vāgbuddhipāṇipādaiś cāpy upetasya vipaścitaḥ kiṃ hīyate manuṣyasya mandasyāpi hi jīvataḥ
english: What is lacking to a man endowed with speech, intellect, hands, and feet, and with discernment—what is lacking even to a dull man, so long as he lives?

sanskrit: jīvan hi kurute pūjāṃ viprāgryaḥ śaśisūryayoḥ bruvann api kathāṃ puṇyāṃ tatra kīṭa tvam eṣyasi
english: While he lives, the foremost of brāhmaṇas offers worship to the moon and the sun, even by reciting a holy tale; to that estate, O worm, you shall come.

sanskrit: guṇabhūtāni bhūtāni tatra tvam upabhokṣyase tatra te 'haṃ vineṣyāmi brahmatvaṃ yatra cecchasi
english: There you shall enjoy creatures of fine quality; there I shall guide you to brāhmaṇa-hood, which you desire.

sanskrit: sa tatheti pratiśrutya kīṭo vartmany atiṣṭhata tam ṛṣiṃ draṣṭum agamat sarvāsv anyāsu yoniṣu
english: Saying "So be it" in assent, the worm stood still upon the track, and in all the other births it underwent it came to behold that seer.

sanskrit: śvāvidgodhāvarāhāṇāṃ tathaiva mṛgapakṣiṇām śvapākavaiśyaśūdrāṇāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca yoniṣu
english: In the wombs of the porcupine, the iguana, and the boar, and likewise of deer and birds, of the dog-cooker, the vaiśya, the śūdra, and the kṣatriya.

sanskrit: sa kīṭety evam ābhāṣya ṛṣiṇā satyavādinā pratismṛtyātha jagrāha pādau mūrdhnā kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Addressed as "worm" by the truth-speaking seer, it remembered its past, and with folded hands and bowed head it grasped his feet.

sanskrit: kīṭa uvāca idaṃ tad atulaṃ sthānam īpsitaṃ daśabhir guṇaiḥ yad ahaṃ prāpya kīṭatvam āgato rājaputratām
english: The worm said: This is that incomparable station, longed for with its tenfold excellences, in that I, who had reached worm-hood, have attained the rank of a king's son.

sanskrit: vahanti mām atibalāḥ kuñjarā hemamālinaḥ syandaneṣu ca kāmbojā yuktāḥ paramavājinaḥ
english: Mighty elephants garlanded with gold bear me, and in my chariots are yoked excellent steeds of the Kāmboja breed.

sanskrit: uṣṭrāśvatarayuktāni yānāni ca vahanti mām sabāndhavaḥ sahāmātyaś cāśnāmi piśitaudanam
english: Carriages yoked with camels and mules bear me, and with my kinsmen and counselors I dine on rice and meat.

sanskrit: gṛheṣu sunivāseṣu sukheṣu śayaneṣu ca parārdhyeṣu mahābhāga svapāmīha supūjitaḥ
english: In well-appointed houses and on comfortable couches of the costliest sort, O blessed one, I sleep here, held in high honor.

sanskrit: sarveṣv apararātreṣu sūtamāgadhabandinaḥ stuvanti māṃ yathā devaṃ mahendraṃ priyavādinaḥ
english: In every last watch of the night the bards, the panegyrists, and the minstrels, sweet-spoken, sing my praises as though I were the god great Indra.

sanskrit: prasādāt satyasaṃdhasya bhavato 'mitatejasaḥ yad ahaṃ kīṭatāṃ prāpya saṃprāpto rājaputratām
english: By the grace of you, true to your word and of measureless splendor, I, who had fallen into worm-hood, have attained the rank of a king's son.

sanskrit: namas te 'stu mahāprājña kiṃ karomi praśādhi mām tvattapobalanirdiṣṭam idaṃ hy adhigataṃ mayā
english: Homage be to you, O greatly wise one; what shall I do? Command me. For this estate has been attained by me as decreed by the power of your austerity.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca arcito 'haṃ tvayā rājan vāgbhir adya yadṛcchayā adya te kīṭatāṃ prāpya smṛtir jātājugupsitā
english: Vyāsa said: I am honored by you, O king, with these unsought words today; today, having passed through worm-hood, an unrevolted memory has arisen in you.

sanskrit: na tu nāśo 'sti pāpasya yat tvayopacitaṃ purā śūdreṇārthapradhānena nṛśaṃsenātatāyinā
english: Yet there is no destruction of the evil that you heaped up of old, when you were a śūdra who set wealth above all, cruel and an aggressor.

sanskrit: mama te darśanaṃ prāptaṃ tac caiva sukṛtaṃ purā tiryagyonau sma jātena mama cāpy arcanāt tathā
english: My sight was gained by you, and that too was a good deed of old; though born in a beast's womb, you yet did me honor.

sanskrit: itas tvaṃ rājaputratvād brāhmaṇyaṃ samavāpsyasi gobrāhmaṇakṛte prāṇān hutvātmīyān raṇājire
english: From this estate of a king's son you shall attain to brāhmaṇa-hood, by offering up your own life in battle for the sake of cows and brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: rājaputrasukhaṃ prāpya ṛtūṃś caivāptadakṣiṇān atha modiṣyase svarge brahmabhūto 'vyayaḥ sukhī
english: Having gained the happiness of a king's son and performed the seasonal rites with their full priestly fees, you shall then rejoice in heaven, become one with Brahman, imperishable and happy.

sanskrit: tiryagyonyāḥ śūdratām abhyupaiti; śūdro vaiśyatvaṃ kṣatriyatvaṃ ca vaiśyaḥ vṛttaślāghī kṣatriyo brāhmaṇatvaṃ; svargaṃ puṇyaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ sādhuvṛttaḥ
english: From the beast's womb one comes to śūdra-hood; the śūdra to vaiśya-hood, and the vaiśya to kṣatriya-hood; the kṣatriya praised for his conduct attains brāhmaṇa-hood, and the brāhmaṇa of righteous conduct attains holy heaven.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kṣatradharmam anuprāptaḥ smarann eva sa vīryavān tyaktvā sa kīṭatāṃ rājaṃś cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Having attained the duty of a kṣatriya, that valiant one, still remembering his past and having cast off worm-hood, O king, practiced abundant austerity.

sanskrit: tasya dharmārthaviduṣo dṛṣṭvā tad vipulaṃ tapaḥ ājagāma dvijaśreṣṭhaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanas tadā
english: Seeing that abundant austerity of his, who knew dharma and gain, the best of the twice-born, Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, then came to him.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca kṣātraṃ caiva vrataṃ kīṭa bhūtānāṃ paripālanam kṣātraṃ caiva vrataṃ dhyāyaṃs tato vipratvam eṣyasi
english: Vyāsa said: The vow of the kṣatriya, O worm, is the guarding of living beings; meditating on that vow of the kṣatriya, you shall thence come to brāhmaṇa-hood.

sanskrit: pāhi sarvāḥ prajāḥ samyak śubhāśubhavid ātmavān śubhaiḥ saṃvibhajan kāmair aśubhānāṃ ca pāvanaiḥ
english: Protect all your subjects rightly, knowing good from evil, self-possessed, dispensing wholesome pleasures and purifying the evildoers.

sanskrit: ātmavān bhava suprītaḥ svadharmacaraṇe rataḥ kṣātrīṃ tanuṃ samutsṛjya tato vipratvam eṣyasi
english: Be self-possessed, well content, delighting in the practice of your own dharma; casting off the kṣatriya body, you shall thence come to brāhmaṇa-hood.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca so 'thāraṇyam abhipretya punar eva yudhiṣṭhira maharṣer vacanaṃ śrutvā prajā dharmeṇa pālya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, O Yudhiṣṭhira, having heard the great seer's word, and having protected his subjects with dharma, he set his mind once more upon the forest.

sanskrit: acireṇaiva kālena kīṭaḥ pārthivasattama prajāpālanadharmeṇa pretya vipratvam āgataḥ
english: In no long time, O best of kings, the worm, by the duty of protecting his subjects, departed this life and came to brāhmaṇa-hood.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā punar eva mahāyaśāḥ ājagāma mahāprājñaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanas tadā
english: Then, seeing him become a brāhmaṇa, the greatly renowned and greatly wise Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana came to him once again.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca bho bho viprarṣabha śrīman mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ kathaṃ cana śubhakṛc chubhayonīṣu pāpakṛt pāpayoniṣu upapadyati dharmajña yathādharmaṃ yathāgamam
english: Vyāsa said: Ho there, O illustrious bull among brāhmaṇas, be not troubled in any way! The doer of good is born into good wombs, the doer of evil into evil wombs, O knower of dharma, each according to his dharma and as the scriptures declare.

sanskrit: tasmān mṛtyubhayāt kīṭa mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ kathaṃ cana dharmalopād bhayaṃ te syāt tasmād dharmaṃ carottamam
english: Therefore, O worm, be not troubled in any way by the fear of death; let your fear be of the lapse from dharma—therefore practice the highest dharma.

sanskrit: kīṭa uvāca sukhāt sukhataraṃ prāpto bhagavaṃs tvatkṛte hy aham dharmamūlāṃ śriyaṃ prāpya pāpmā naṣṭa ihādya me
english: The worm said: I have attained, O blessed one, a happiness happier than happiness, through your doing; having gained prosperity rooted in dharma, my sin is this day destroyed in me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca bhagavadvacanāt kīṭo brāhmaṇyaṃ prāpya durlabham akarot pṛthivīṃ rājan yajñayūpaśatāṅkitām tataḥ sālokyam agamad brahmaṇo brahmavittamaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: At the word of the blessed sage, the worm, having attained the hard-won state of a brāhmaṇa, made the earth marked with a hundred sacrificial posts, O king; thereafter, that best of knowers of Brahman went to share the world of Brahman.

sanskrit: avāpa ca paraṃ kīṭaḥ pārtha brahma sanātanam svakarmaphalanirvṛttaṃ vyāsasya vacanāt tadā
english: And the worm attained, O Pārtha, the supreme eternal Brahman, brought about by the fruit of his own deeds and by the word of Vyāsa.

sanskrit: te 'pi yasmāt svabhāvena hatāḥ kṣatriyapuṃgavāḥ saṃprāptās te gatiṃ puṇyāṃ tasmān mā śoca putraka
english: Since those bulls among kṣatriyas too were slain in accordance with their very nature, they have attained a holy destiny; therefore do not grieve, my son.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca vidyā tapaś ca dānaṃ ca kim eteṣāṃ viśiṣyate pṛcchāmi tvā satāṃ śreṣṭha tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Sacred learning, austerity, and giving—which of these is the most excellent? I ask you, O best of the good; tell me that, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam maitreyasya ca saṃvādaṃ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recount an ancient tale—the dialogue of Maitreya and Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇadvaipāyano rājann ajñātacaritaṃ caran vārāṇasyām upātiṣṭhan maitreyaṃ svairiṇīkule
english: Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, O king, while wandering in disguise unrecognized, came to attend upon Maitreya at Vārāṇasī, in the dwelling of a wanton woman.

sanskrit: tam upasthitam āsīnaṃ jñātvā sa munisattamam arcitvā bhojayām āsa maitreyo 'śanam uttamam
english: Knowing that best of sages had come and was seated before him, Maitreya honored him and fed him excellent food.

sanskrit: tad annam uttamaṃ bhuktvā guṇavat sārvakāmikam pratiṣṭhamāno 'smayata prītaḥ kṛṣṇo mahāmanāḥ
english: Having eaten that excellent food, of fine quality and satisfying every desire, the great-souled Kṛṣṇa, well pleased, smiled as he made ready to depart.

sanskrit: tam utsmayantaṃ saṃprekṣya maitreyaḥ kṛṣṇam abravīt kāraṇaṃ brūhi dharmātman yo 'smayiṣṭhāḥ kutaś ca te tapasvino dhṛtimataḥ pramodaḥ samupāgataḥ
english: Beholding him smiling, Maitreya said to Kṛṣṇa: Tell me the reason, O righteous one, why you smiled; and whence has this joy come upon you, an ascetic firm of resolve?
